transcript.text: I found out my broke client is actually
loaded and now I feel like an idiot. I
gave this client 30% off my rate because
she told me she was a struggling solo
entrepreneur. Turns out she sold a
company 2 years ago and is sitting on
serious money. Do I confront her or is
there a better way to handle clients who
play you like this?
>> I mean, you said you were willing to do
it for 30% less, so why does her story
even matter? If that business decision
made sense for you at 30% off, then it
made sense for you at 30% off. Like the
end result is the same.
>> The real thing here is that I think you
are ashamed of the fact that you didn't
have integrity with yourself about your
own pricing. The idea of broke clients,
rich clients, I'm a believer in being an
equal opportunity salesman because
everyone's money is green. And so
whether someone tells a sob story or
they're rich as hell, I have a price
that I'm willing to do something for and
their their money spends the same. At
the end of the day, like it's a
business, you have a price, you have
value, you made an exchange. None of
that changed. And so I think if you're
unhappy with the price, raise your
prices. Or stick to the price you really
want.
